capabilities.compatibility: No API or schema change. Additive complete output inventory and attachment-only downloads; existing cleanup types remain unchanged. Restart succeeds only after an authenticated loopback check observes a new PID serving current disk source. Existing LaunchAgent selection and restart API remain compatible. Keep single and multiple selection modes, existing document-generator values, the attach/setValue/setDisabled contract, and the apex:client-change/open/error events during migration. Preserve native input values in YYYY-MM-DD form.

Keep light, dark, and user color theme propagation across iframes. One transparent PNG or WebP logo is shared across color themes. The global tab bar brand button replaces the visible main tab and invokes the same switchTab('main') action; mobile retains its separate home button. The native brandIcon handler accepts only local application pages and changes the running Dock icon. Other uploads are rendered with the same inset rounded canvas and packaged through the same multiresolution iconset pipeline before the running Dock icon changes. Keep the existing bundle identifier so WebKit data and macOS permissions remain available. The native client publishes its active logo into ignored data/mobile-brand.json; authenticated settings changes also publish it. Public GET /api/brand and /brand-logo.png contain only branding, while PUT /api/brand requires existing authentication. Mobile clients retain the last logo locally for offline startup, refresh it on connection and foreground, and render dark variants with the shared adapter. Manifest id remains /case-manager and start_url is /; existing iOS home icons may require re-adding the shortcut. Shell v232 refreshes branding without deleting case caches or pending operations.

Preserve Finder copy/paste, upload, download, and private-mode restrictions. Local file list and search responses may add Finder tag metadata; the case-files page and AI file picker render the seven macOS tag colors, while the case-files context menu may update the selected file or folder's Finder tag color and recursively apply it to descendants when a folder is selected. Scanner case imports reuse store_case_file with download_material under #下载材料, retain source metadata and the existing import response, and validate the binding before retrieval and again at write. Judicial-delivery archive folders default to #Stella电子送达归档 and the Important/red Finder tag on creation or legacy migration; reuse the Finder metadata helpers, preserve other tags and later user edits, and do not tag descendants by default. Court-service tests isolate default downloads and browser profiles in anonymous temporary directories.

Existing business download/export routes remain compatible. Unified authenticated metadata is atomically persisted under runtime data, with bounded 2000-record history and at most three managed jobs. Seven sources share honest real-byte/unknown-size progress and case/path context; court dossiers retain their durable executor. Invoice scans cover all selectable IMAP folders with account/folder-scoped caches and paths, bounded complete-range continuation, isolated invoice summaries and UIDVALIDITY reset handling; signed amounts and explicit invoice identity drive selection/totals; exports preserve all selected files within a documented bound and serialize history repair/write; browser view revisions reject stale account responses; scan warnings and timeouts propagate as partial completion to downloads and monthly collection. Mail invoice vs case vs other is explicit; case writes require confirmation and currently available folder binding. Normal mail collection no longer writes into invoice folders. Legacy browser history imports idempotently and only locates exact existing Downloads basenames, never infers a case. File paths cannot be assigned by client PATCH; native user-selected paths must match a known downloaded artifact byte for byte. Native ZIP transfers retain streaming without a browser memory ceiling. Cleaning completed records never deletes files or hides unassigned case materials. Native WKDownload byte observations report actual save-panel paths; apex:open-download-source version 1 routes only requests from a registered download-center frame to an allowlisted existing feature; relaunch is required to activate a rebuilt native shell. New progress assets are data-free public shell resources; business endpoints remain authenticated. Invoice recognition v6 prefers labelled capital totals over PDF drawing order and reconciles exact invoice identities against XML, including same-message same-basename outlined OFDs. Trip itineraries remain downloadable supporting files and are excluded from default invoice selection and totals. Date-verified historical local inbox files supplement the server IMAP window without changing mail. Thirty-second scan batches continue automatically with view-revision guards and bounded retries; failed messages remain pending. Same-account lock waits are bounded. Scan interruption uses scan-specific progress text. Invoice scan v4 applies a decoded 5 MiB hard limit and a 1 MiB hint-based soft filter, preserving small XMLs. BODYSTRUCTURE manifests permit bounded readonly PEEK section fetches so oversized siblings stay on the server; cached files, ZIP members and local history use the same filter without deleting originals. Download-center v4 adds source panels for cases, archives, knowledge, calculators, recordings, scanner, expenses, filing and settings. Explicit download anchors (including detached programmatic clicks) use the shared adapter; preview/navigation links and streamed dossier ZIPs retain existing behavior. Size sorting and bounds use actual disk bytes across the full filtered set; unknown sizes sort last. Inclusive Shanghai date filters use created_at. Analysis distinguishes missing files with accessible parent directories from unavailable volumes, unknown locations and batch-only records. Confirmed cleanup rechecks selected IDs and hides only missing inactive records. Explicit file deletion uses Finder Trash, record IDs and file revisions; errors remain visible and unchanged/active files are protected. No live data is removed by analysis. Glass workspace uses grouped source navigation, on-demand filters and selection-only bulk tools. confirmAction accepts an optional explicit confirmLabel; source links name the destination page and do not imply automatic retry. PWA shell 263 caches the updated shared adapter.
Keep record IDs routable from macOS notifications.

New events use the apex:* namespace and include a version when their payload is not trivial. The archive picker inside case-files uses apex:archive-picker-ready, apex:archive-selection, and apex:archive-assign-request with version 1, caseId, and relative file paths; the archive workbench replies with apex:archive-status or apex:archive-clear-selection for the same caseId. Knowledge center uses apex:knowledge-prefill-ask with version 1 and question; the parent checks same origin and the source knowledge tab iframe before filling AI Ask. apex:open-court-downloads carries version 1 and optional jobId; the main host validates same origin and a court-online or download-center source iframe before opening the progress tab.

The apex:page-visibility message is version 1; host tab selection is independent from document visibility, so foreground recovery resumes only selected pages; overview cards remain visible without CSS entry animations; inactive pages may pause work but must preserve drafts. Low-risk read-only pages may be hibernated after their state is captured; editors, recordings, uploads, CAPTCHA flows and other unsafe pages remain mounted until they implement an explicit snapshot contract. File pages close subscriptions while inactive and share backend directory watchers; automation screenshots and polling pause while inactive. Interval callbacks serialize Promise-returning work. Visibility messages validate parent and same origin.

The public shell contains no case data. Keep the Service Worker scope and /case-manager entry stable, preserve the legal-kb-case-manager IndexedDB schema and pending case-operation queue, validate shell responses before caching, and never clear user data during shell repair. Verified top-level /case-manager navigation enters /?workspace=cases, reusing the existing main tab host and mobile floating navigation; iframe case navigation is never redirected. The public /app-shell endpoint exposes only source UI markup, and its required static assets are public; business APIs remain authenticated. Offline root navigation ignores query parameters and uses a verified home cache; online login responses remain authoritative. Shell 257 uses the existing Efficiency Center registry in a full-viewport mobile dialog with category shortcuts, one content scroller, focus containment, reversible background inert state and viewport/keyboard resizing. Touch devices through 1024px also use this layout in landscape; desktop retains an anchored menu. Ordering and subtitle preference contracts stay unchanged. Shell 256 fixes the sidebar-directory asset version mismatch that interrupted offline startup and aligns the case script worker registration with the host to prevent WebKit update races. Entry-page script and stylesheet URLs are checked against the worker cache manifest. Phone case-detail actions wrap within the drawer, titles clamp to two lines, toasts clear host navigation, and the shell uses dynamic viewport height. Tabbed AI panels use their containing pane width, wrap tools, and overlay history on narrow tablets. Shell 255 publishes versioned generated bootstrap, lazy AI chunk, feature loader and minified CSS; offline installation includes the lazy chunk. Source app.js/style.css remain compatible public artifacts. Case snapshots hydrate details in batches within one query-only snapshot; duplicate client requests share one Promise. Regular native navigation revalidates HTML without clearing caches or user data. Shell 281 refreshes dismissal styles, tag candidate icons, list request ordering and editor acknowledgement handling. Case/reminder list responses may render only for the latest request and original tab; article saves use the acknowledged title as the next conflict baseline and refresh their owning reading surface. Shell 282 restores desktop/mobile efficiency header visibility, right-aligned edit actions and mobile close typography. Model/source/skill popups share a panel-scoped containing block, visible-viewport bounds, resize handling and compatible delegated selection/outside-click behavior. Narrow AI workspaces start with overlay history closed; welcome cards are bounded to their chat pane. Direct settings navigation scrolls the selected category into view using layout rather than scaled animation pixels. Static authentication/error responses, redirects and HTML never receive immutable asset caching; successful versioned assets retain their prior cache policy.

articles.domains remains the top-level JSON list. GET /api/domains keeps domain and count fields and adds id and children. Article list and detail responses add subcategories with id, name, parent_id and domain alongside subcategory_ids; main article cards and both reader metadata bars display confirmed child labels, with cached catalog resolution for older offline snapshots. Both readers keep source, author, date and label editing outside the collapsible classification labels, visible in both disclosure states with single-line truncation on narrow screens. Main cards and both reader metadata bars share a single-row 2:1 label/provenance layout. Overflow labels animate open on pointer hover and close on leave; a button also pins expansion for touch and keyboard, Escape collapses, and ResizeObserver remeasures wrapping. List provenance includes author, date and source with independent source actions. List root, child and custom label buttons reuse chooseDirectoryFilter with exact identities, clear search and health filters, reset pagination and never open the article; reader labels remain informational. Rules cover every predefined domain and known historical roots, with AI fallback evaluated per domain; migration 16 backfills historical child-topic evidence without changing article assignments. Rules and configured AI discover child suggestions from new and historical articles; known related phrases are consolidated into reusable topics, and automatic proposals enter the review list and can be approved only when at least two distinct articles support a concise topic. Original single-article proposals remain stored. No suggestion enters the approved taxonomy without confirmation. User-selected and excluded classifications and child order survive automatic re-evaluation; source URLs remain article metadata. Deleting a child taxonomy node removes only its article associations, preserves the articles, and suppresses future automatic proposals with the same name under that parent; explicit manual creation clears the suppression. Root deletion remains a separate flow. The unified directory manager owns professional/custom/author editing, with explicit drag handles, insertion boundaries, edge scrolling and Alt/Option keyboard ordering; root dragging temporarily hides child rows and restores them on drop or cancellation without changing expansion preferences; legacy open functions remain adapters. Child rename preserves IDs, keywords and article associations and suppresses old automatic proposals. Reorder requests validate a complete current visible collection and return 409 atomically on duplicates or stale IDs. Offline article snapshot v3 adds subcategory_ids and classification_status without changing IndexedDB keys; older snapshots remain usable for general browsing, but child/pending filters require v3 and the relevant fields. Saved views accept optional subcategoryId, clear absent or deleted child IDs, and retain the parent domain. Expansion mode and paths use the safely parsed legal_kb_directory_state_v1 preference; hovering a root reveals its next level, while hovering a specific child reveals only its own descendants after pointer intent detection; search expansion is temporary. Reclassification preview adds has_changes and subcategory_add/remove by comparing effective assignments, respecting manual selections and exclusions. Matching an existing child or requesting AI alone is not a change. Batched apply skips unchanged articles and adds scanned alongside processed and next_after_id.

Collect aggregate local metrics only; never retain URLs with queries, request bodies, client names, file paths, or case content. Additive metrics may include current and peak memory, aggregate child-process usage, thread/task counts, hibernated-page counts, and coarse case-manager startup stage/timing; child command-line arguments are never collected.

OpenCode Grok 4.7 uses stateless Responses with local history replay, no remote storage, answer-only deltas, terminal-event validation and normalized choices/usage for both foreground and background callers. Existing Chat Completions models retain their route. CC2API is additive. cc2api: model IDs use the official Claude Code headless client for Claude Code-only key groups and normalize JSON results into the existing choices contract. The pinned client lives in ignored data/cc2api-runtime; scripts/install_cc2api_runtime.py installs it. Per-call temporary configuration, bare mode, no built-in or MCP tools, and no session persistence isolate the client. Cancellation and timeout kill the child. Keys remain in private config and child environment only. Existing defaults and fallback behavior remain compatible. Official DeepSeek Flash displays V4.1 Flash 1017 while keeping the rolling deepseek-flash ID and old-ID migrations. OpenCode Go retains its provider-specific label until its served snapshot is verified; no default route or hidden-model preference changes. Direct modes direct_ai and direct_ai_web return before KB/MCP routing, use separate conversation history, and reuse the public web adapter from case_files for every provider. Direct web mode plans bounded queries with current Shanghai date and recent user context, retrieves through a shared multi-engine adapter, checks entity/topic relevance, follows validated HTTP/meta redirects, and records retrieval time. Only actual relevant public web results are returned as external_sources; search failure is explicit and the retrieval budget is 45 seconds. New Doubao 2.1 0915 model IDs are additive and require Ark activation; the stable Mini alias now uses verified 260428. AI workspace balance reuses the existing provider balance route, maps model options by catalog provider ID, and displays only supported successful finite balances. Visible workspaces refresh serially every 30 seconds and on model changes, foreground return and answer completion; hidden pages abort requests. Unsupported providers and failures hide the badge; stale responses from earlier selections are ignored. Direct AI can deliver bounded fenced HTML/SVG/CSV/JSON/TXT/Markdown artifacts. Additive artifacts descriptors are derived from existing answer text on response and history load, requiring no schema change. The existing message export route accepts optional artifact_index for exact file bytes, including Markdown/TXT to Word conversion. HTML/SVG previews use a sandboxed frame, restrictive CSP and stripped navigation/active elements; original downloadable contents remain intact. Existing whole-answer Markdown/Word exports and unified download staging are retained. Public web evidence is selected locally by topic coverage with original figures, table rows and adjacent qualifications; duplicate passages and URLs are removed. Evidence uses an adaptive 4/7/12 KB UTF-8 ceiling, reduced further to the foreground request remaining budget. No summarization model or raw full pages are added to the final prompt; source markers only advertise represented passages and partial topic coverage is explicit. Identity/greeting-only requests skip search planning. Other web planning is bounded to eight seconds and 450 output tokens; local fallback preserves explicit domains, dotted API names and immediate follow-up context. Invalid provider response envelopes and remote protocol failures enter the existing fallback chain. Both file-question routes provide complete extracted texts whenever the model/request budget permits, without the old 18-span cap. Longer inputs are scanned locally using query BM25, generic typographic/numbered headings and adaptive marginal relevance with duplicate and positional diversity, allocated in fair rounds per file. No document-type-specific section whitelist or extra model calls are used. Original spans retain adjacent conditions and inherited section labels with index-relative character locators; if even one span per file cannot fit the request fails explicitly. Incremental duplicate/position scoring avoids rescanning all previous selections. Both parsing and evidence selection run off the event loop for synchronous work; selection copies request context into the worker and cooperatively stops on cancellation. Optional external evidence is admitted only within the fully framed remaining input/output budget, and rejected evidence has no source cards. Missing/invalid model citations fall back to one card per distinct file; source identifiers disambiguate equal filenames. Per-file supplied/extracted character counts enter the model prompt and research trace; partial retrieval is visible and cannot be treated as absence in the original file. FILE markers identify spans rather than independent documents; file errors/cancellation are recorded before FastAPI converts them to HTTP responses, so recovery does not wait forever on received state. Judicial messages and hearing notices use independently configurable purpose models. SMS settings mirror that same preference instead of keeping a competing model source. Custom Chat Completions/Responses providers use owner-only ignored runtime JSON, namespaced allowlisted model IDs, credential-free catalog payloads and shared streaming/stateless Responses transports. OpenAI/Kimi setup presets leave model IDs to the account owner. Provider/model removal invalidates stale defaults and purpose overrides; unknown custom IDs fail closed. The existing allowed-model set object is retained across runtime reload for all imported consumers. Runtime config-directory lookup is canonical for local/public builds.

capabilities.compatibility: Reuses the existing AI chat DOM, models, exports and request cancellation. SQL authorizer permits only case-related tables and non-secret columns, bounded read queries and aggregates on a consistent SQLite snapshot. All synced court-online records, including unmatched cases, filing audits, hearings, delivery messages and raw JSON fields are available; sync timestamps and multiple accounts must be distinguished. Case-linked research projects, ledgers, memo entries, notes, questions, search runs, personal income, reading records and project-linked articles are available through recursive ownership discovery. All-case snapshots retain unlinked court records but remove unbound research and unrelated articles. AI histories and research answers are secondary working records, not verified facts. Focused requests preload project-owned memo/ledger/notes text with citation links before model planning; large results and long text require pagination. Basic case memo is distinct from drawer memo entries. Final JSON answer envelopes are unwrapped on every backend path; historical envelopes are normalized for rendering, copying and export. No live portal fetch or database writes. Existing AI_ASK sources remain compatible. Specific case evidence carries case_links and opens a case_id deep link in the shared case detail drawer. Old clipped JSON sources are normalized at display time; case-only controls are hidden and tables retain readable minimum column widths. Case-only shortcuts prefill editable questions without sending requests or mutating case data. Active/archived and 7/30/90-day controls affect generated questions only; unmatched court records remain a separate review list. Empty conversations show the welcome shortcuts only. After the first message, the shortcuts move to a collapsible composer toolbar; returning to an empty conversation or leaving case mode removes it. Styles remain scoped to the case AI workspace in the existing stylesheet, preserving offline shell asset paths. Optional caseId/caseTitle in the case_database context separate focused histories and add a case-specific instruction to every request without changing the read-only query API. POST /api/ask accepts optional focus_case_id for case_database. Focused requests materialize a read-only in-memory snapshot containing only the selected case, actual series children and explicitly owned records (including foreign-key descendants); unfiltered SQL and aggregates cannot reach other cases. Unlinked court records and tables without an ownership path are unavailable in this scope and require separate review. Timeline requests use structured cited events, sorted by validated dates with unknown dates and system records in separate sections. The focus and todo review dialogs reuse ApexCasePicker. Answer excerpts can prefill editable notes; only explicit draft confirmation calls the existing POST /api/case-manager/todos, with no inferred dates or completion status.

Migration 21 adds scoped personal/case memories, immutable provenance, revisions and suppression tombstones, post-upgrade message eligibility, persistent bounded background jobs and per-conversation summaries/exclusions. Stable message upserts and optimistic save versions preserve existing history contracts. history_key/current_message_id and context_usage are additive across workspace/file routes; legacy conversation_context remains supported. No historical mining/backfill. Per-turn no-memory blocks durable capture and cross-chat recall permanently for those messages while retaining same-chat context. Case isolation requires an existing explicit ID; mixed-case sessions stay noncase and do not borrow case memories. Summaries/history are background data, never legal evidence. Conservative configurable UTF-8 token upper-bound budgets reject oversized prompts explicitly. Deletion/disable/version guards prevent in-flight writes resurrecting old data. Offline shell assets are versioned together. Audit migration 22 separates history optimistic revisions from context settings, propagates no-memory through derived responses, repairs eligible old taint chains and persists per-job capture consent. Summary-only jobs work with auto-capture disabled. Claim generations protect running rebuilds; rebuild retries failed plus latest work instead of re-mining all completed turns. Visible request state projects a conversation-keyed task map (four concurrent generations), with per-task cancellation, stable answer ownership, bounded multi-marker recovery and conversation drafts. Memory/context sheets use shared glass tokens, a scrollable reading area and persistent actions. Selected personal Skills load only their complete core file (48 KB bound), never their installation tree; basic identity/memory/greeting questions skip irrelevant task instructions. Official deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro use a conservative 64,000 application ceiling; unknown/gateway models retain 24,000 and explicit deployment overrides remain authoritative. Persisted Skill IDs are validated before send and selected state remains visible while the list loads; oversized mandatory Skill instructions return an actionable 413 before the provider call. Live-message deletion and regeneration are blocked during that conversation generation; failed/stopped answers remain ineligible for memory. Terminal stream errors are stored with their real cause, while actual connection losses use progress recovery. Cancellation requires a successful JSON acknowledgement rather than HTTP 200 alone.

Packaging only; existing runtime and APIs stay unchanged. No existing database, uploads, financial records, local credentials, browser sessions, user Skills or Git history. Team identity, contact, bank and real client defaults are sanitized in the build snapshot. Raw backend Python source files are removed after freezing. Original sample articles and fictional cases seed once; deleted examples never return. Dedicated loopback port and runtime/config directories. Default distribution branding uses the user-authorized current logo. Canonical frontend styles are packaged without preview overrides. Brand preferences live in the independent runtime directory; first native launch reads the default before publishing. Public distribution alone omits the personal-finance catalog entry, settings section, page, backend module and Feishu family-finance routes. All other feature code is retained, including local OCR dependencies and the user manual. Ad-hoc signed arm64 or x86_64 app, built with a matching Python and isolated dependencies; no notarization claimed. Every packaged Mach-O must support the target architecture. Intel uses appcast-intel.xml, Apple Silicon uses appcast.xml; mixed-architecture update directories are rejected. Public updater-enabled builds require macOS 12 and Sparkle 2.10.0, keep app identity/runtime separate, own graceful backend shutdown and back up SQLite before build changes. Ed25519 key stays in Keychain; app-only ZIPs and verified signed deltas/full fallback use Pages feed and immutable Releases assets. Optional consented content-free heartbeats go to Workers/D1, with generated high-entropy administrator password and signed host-only session cookies; no Cloudflare Access subscription. Metric definitions distinguish asset requests, reporting first launches and six-hour sampled active devices. Server telemetry conditionally saves each installation at most once per rolling six hours in an atomic D1 batch; duplicates write zero rows while indexed reads/HTTP requests remain. Compatible summary online means six-hour activity; daily activity and version/OS are sampled. Existing client timers remain 60 seconds pending the next authorized installer release; remind the owner to change them to six hours before that release. A Pages entrance uses a private Service Binding to retain the same Worker authentication, rate limiting and D1 data without client workers.dev resolution; explicit HTML asset routing preserves upstream errors. See docs/PUBLIC_UPDATES_AND_ADMIN.md. Fada page/crawler are explicit shipped public resources; notes and refreshed data stay in the recipient runtime. Every generated package verifies all discovered HTML entry routes and local static references, plus populated Fada APIs. Mac Contacts, Calendar and Vision helpers are precompiled for the package architecture; recipient developer tools are not required.

Existing synchronous download route remains compatible, with additive progress result and authenticated progress GET. Actual decoded byte counts, unknown-size indeterminate state, per-file saved/failed counters and honest partial failure. Bounded in-memory snapshots, duplicate download prevention and serial polling only in visible active drawer. Restart clears progress; business files and database are unchanged.

Additive per-record shortcuts for todos, hearings, preservations and appeals. No case folder binding changes or file copies; exclusive foreign keys cascade metadata only. Authenticated local desktop access remains allowed in private mode; loopback peer/target, local Origin and no proxy forwarding headers are required. Authentication stays in middleware. Additive local member metadata scoped by account/folder/UID, checked against summary date/from/subject to avoid reused UID labels. Atomic bulk writes; surviving cache eviction and restart. Deleted members retain prior display names/filtering; new assignments validate current member IDs. Filters apply to loaded summaries and compose with existing filters. No IMAP flag, read state or email transmission changes.

Only local access-gate 401 responses carry X-Apex-Auth-Required: local. Legacy plain Authentication required and local login HTML remain supported. Integration JSON 401 and other business 4xx preserve messages without login navigation or offline fallback. Session-status still controls actual session recovery; no protected endpoint is made public.
